description: The Spreadsheet validation alert used for both the Stop-style error and the Warning/Information confirm. It is a modal alertdialog: the core TmFocusScope supplies the role, aria-modal, the accessible name (aria-labelledby) and description (aria-describedby), the initial focus on the primary action, the document-level Escape and the focus restore on close. A Stop alert is a hard block — the value is rejected and only the primary action or Escape dismisses it (a backdrop click does nothing); the confirm also cancels on the backdrop or the cancel action. Ids are per instance and not a selector contract; key off [role='alertdialog'] inside .tm-spreadsheet.

parameters.name: Title
parameters.description: The alert title (the rule's own title, or the localized default).

parameters.name: Message
parameters.description: The alert body text (the rule's own message, or the localized default).

parameters.name: IsStop
parameters.description: True for the Stop style: the value is blocked, so a backdrop click does nothing and there is no cancel path.

parameters.name: PrimaryText
parameters.description: Label of the primary action (Confirm / Yes).

parameters.name: CancelText
parameters.description: Label of the cancel action. Only rendered when ShowCancel is true.

parameters.name: ShowCancel
parameters.description: Whether a cancel action exists. False for a Stop alert, true for the confirm.

parameters.name: RestoreFocusTargetId
parameters.description: The id of the element focus returns to when the alert closes — the host spreadsheet passes its grid root, so focus lands on the grid rather than the toolbar button that opened the alert. Null falls back to the element focused before the alert opened.

parameters.name: RestoreFocus
parameters.description: Whether closing the alert restores the focus it took. Defaults to true.

parameters.name: OnPrimary
parameters.description: Raised when the user accepts the alert (the only close path of a Stop alert).

parameters.name: OnCancel
parameters.description: Raised when the user cancels the alert (a backdrop click or the cancel action).
